title: 29-layer HfO2/MgF2 UV bandpass with index-dependent thickness bounds and curvature regularization
scientific_hypothesis: A 29-layer HfO2/MgF2 alternating stack with a central cavity defect, optimized under index-dependent thickness perturbation bounds (±1.0 nm edge, ±3.0 nm center) and curvature regularization (weight 0.15), will achieve higher best_target_score than uniform perturbation optimization while maintaining physically valid candidates.
design_principle: Quarter-wave dielectric mirrors with a half-wave or defect layer at the center create a transmission bandpass within a high-reflectance stopband. HfO2 provides high refractive index contrast with MgF2 in the UV-visible range. Constraining thickness adjustments prevents the optimizer from introducing high-frequency oscillations that degrade spectral coherence. Edge layers primarily set broadband reflectance, while central layers tune the passband position and width.
proposed_topology: 29 layers total: layer 1-14 alternating HfO2/MgF2 starting with HfO2, layer 15 is HfO2 cavity defect, layer 16-29 alternating MgF2/HfO2 ending with HfO2. Substrate is sio2 (fused silica), incidence medium is air.
design_variables: individual layer thicknesses in nm with position-dependent bounds: layers 0-3 and 25-28 bounded to ±1.0 nm from QWOT baseline, layers 10-18 bounded to ±3.0 nm from QWOT baseline, intermediate layers bounded to ±2.5 nm from QWOT baseline; curvature regularization weight 0.15 applied to second-difference of thickness vector
soft_objectives: maintain physical validity of all candidates
manufacturing_considerations: total layer count fixed at 29 (within 30-layer limit)
HfO2 and MgF2 are conventional e-beam or thermal evaporation materials
thickness bounds reflect realistic deposition control precision
theory_basis: Recalled knowledge: Quarter-wave stacks produce high reflectance outside the design wavelength; a central defect layer creates a transmission peak within the stopband.
Recalled knowledge: HfO2 has refractive index approximately 2.0-2.2 in UV-visible range; MgF2 has refractive index approximately 1.38-1.42.
Recalled knowledge: Optimization with tight thickness bounds prevents non-manufacturable designs and maintains spectral coherence.
Recalled knowledge: Curvature regularization on thickness vectors reduces high-frequency oscillations that cause scattering losses and fabrication difficulty.
Recalled knowledge: Edge layers in a bandpass filter primarily control out-of-band rejection; central layers tune passband position and width.
expected_advantages: Position-dependent bounds allow more flexibility where it matters most (central cavity region) while stabilizing edge layers that control broadband rejection.
Curvature regularization should reduce oscillatory thickness patterns that appeared in prior iterations.
Maintaining the same material pair and layer count isolates the effect of optimization constraint changes from material or topology changes.
known_risks: Uncertain whether ±1.0 nm edge bounds are too restrictive for achieving target scores; may need relaxation if best_target_score stagnates.
Uncertain whether curvature weight 0.15 is optimal; this value is recalled from general regularization practice, not specific thin-film optimization literature.
Refractive index dispersion of HfO2 and MgF2 below 300 nm is uncertain from memory; actual n/k values will come from the material registry datasets.
The exact quarter-wave optical thickness baseline for 255-280 nm center wavelength is approximate from recalled knowledge; the optimizer will refine from there.
What would settle these: lookup of HfO2 and MgF2 dispersion data in the 250-1100 nm range, review of thin-film optimization regularization literature for recommended curvature weights.
execution_request_english: Optimize a 29-layer planar multilayer thin film stack on fused silica substrate with air incidence. Layer sequence: layers 1-14 alternate HfO2 and MgF2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos) starting with HfO2 (odd layers HfO2, even layers MgF2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos)), layer 15 is HfO2 cavity defect, layers 16-29 alternate MgF2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos) and HfO2 ending with HfO2 (odd layers MgF2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos), even layers HfO2 in this section). Substrate material is SiO2 (Gao). Optimize individual layer thicknesses with position-dependent bounds relative to quarter-wave optical thickness baseline at 267.5 nm center wavelength: layers 0-3 and 25-28 (0-indexed) bounded to ±1.0 nm, layers 10-18 bounded to ±3.0 nm, all other layers bounded to ±2.5 nm. Apply curvature regularization with weight 0.15 to the second-difference of the thickness vector. Spectral objectives: maximize transmittance in 255-280 nm, minimize transmittance in 300-700 nm, minimize transmittance in 700-1100 nm. Total layer count fixed at 29. No metal layers. Use gradient-based thickness optimization.
revision_reason: Continuation of control_route_01 implementing feedback directives: clamped per-layer thickness adjustments to ±2.5 nm envelope with index-dependent decay schedule (edge layers ±1.0 nm, central stack ±3.0 nm), and integrated curvature regularization term weighted at 0.15 to prevent high-frequency oscillatory deviations.
